onboarding.step2Sub: More detail means more specific exercises.
onboarding.injuryPlaceholder:
Include: what happened, when (days/weeks ago), exact location, any surgery/diagnosis, current pain (0-10), what makes it better/worse...

e.g. ACL reconstruction 10 days ago, right knee. Full weight-bearing with crutches OK. Pain 3/10 rest, 6/10 stairs. Significant swelling. Pre-injury: running 40km/week.

tutorial.welcomeBody: Your AI-generated rehab plan is ready. Here's a quick tour — under 30 seconds.
tutorial.exercisesBody: Tap any exercise card on Home to see step-by-step instructions. Tap the circle to mark it done.
tutorial.hydrationBody: Tap a glass to log it. Aim for 8 a day — your tissues heal faster when hydrated.
tutorial.scheduleBody: Open the calendar tab to see all your sessions for the week and reorder them around your life.
tutorial.progressBody: The chart tab tracks pain, mobility and adherence so you can see your recovery curve.
tutorial.chatBody: Stuck on a movement or have a flare-up? The chat tab gives you 24/7 recovery guidance grounded in your plan.

dayComplete.title: Day complete
dayComplete.body: Recovery happens between sessions. Hydrate, sleep well — your body's doing the rest of the work tonight.

streak.msg_3: Three sessions in a row. Your brain is starting to expect this — the habit is taking root.
streak.msg_7: Seven days of showing up. The hardest part of any habit is the start — you cleared it.
streak.msg_14: Recovery is compounding. Two weeks of consistent work is when real tissue change kicks in.
streak.msg_30: A full month. Your nervous system has rewired around movement. Keep going — this is how lasting recovery is built.
streak.msg_60: Two months of daily care for your body. This is athlete-tier discipline.
streak.msg_100: A hundred days. Whatever brought you here is far behind you now.

disclaimer.title: Important — please read
disclaimer.body:
Bloom AI is a wellness and education tool for general recovery guidance only. It does not diagnose, treat, or replace professional medical care. Always consult a qualified clinician about your injury, especially before starting, stopping, or changing any exercise.

If you experience severe pain, loss of function, numbness, sudden swelling, fever, or any emergency symptom, seek immediate medical attention.

adaptation.detectHighPain: Pain has been {{avg}}/10 for {{days}} days in a row.
adaptation.detectTrendingUp: Pain is trending up ({{avg}}/10 vs earlier this week).
adaptation.detectReadyToProgress: Pain has been low for {{days}} days — you may be ready to push harder.
adaptation.kindDeEscalateBody: Your body is telling us the current phase is too much right now. We'll cut intensity by ~25%, swap the loading work for isometric and range-of-motion variants, and extend this phase by a week.
adaptation.kindModifyBody: Pain is creeping up. We'll swap the heaviest exercises for lower-load alternatives while keeping the phase structure — a soft correction, not a rebuild.
adaptation.kindProgressBody: You've earned a harder plan. We'll advance the phase early and upgrade the top loading exercises to the next progression.
adaptation.errFallback: Something went wrong. Try again later.

plan.safetyNote: Evidence-based protocol. Post-surgical: follow your surgeon's restrictions first. Stop any exercise causing sharp pain.
plan.adjustModalBody: Describe what to change. Examples: "no pool exercises, no gym equipment", "make week 1 lighter", "I don't have a foam roller".
plan.errOffTopicFallback: Please describe the change in terms of your recovery.

exercise.stopSeeDoctor: Stop and see a doctor if
